tenant_types.label: Hyperscaler (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Oracle, Amazon)

price_usd_mw_yr_colo.source: Hut 8 Beacon Point $9.8B/352MW/15yr = ~$1.86M/MW/yr base term; Applied Digital Forge tranches ~$0.7-1M+/MW/yr

price_multiplier_compute_bundled.note: compute-inclusive deals (GPU cloud, not pure colo) run 5-10x higher per MW because GPU/compute revenue dominates -- IREN-Microsoft implies ~$9.7M/MW/yr but that is NOT a colo comparable

prepayment_pct.note: not typically required directly -- hyperscalers are creditworthy enough; prepayment appears when the counterparty is a neocloud intermediary, not the hyperscaler itself

tenant_types.sla_penalty: high take-or-pay, liquidated damages for late delivery, standard in all disclosed deals
tenant_types.default_behavior: none observed 2022-2026; hyperscalers have not defaulted or renegotiated down -- they are the credit anchor of the ecosystem

tenant_types.label: AI lab (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI)

prepayment_pct.note: some deals include equity-for-commitment structures instead (OpenAI took CoreWeave warrants)

tenant_types.sla_penalty: same take-or-pay language as hyperscaler deals, but weaker ultimate counterparty credit -- flagged repeatedly by rating agencies and short-sellers (e.g. Kerrisdale on CoreWeave) as the key backlog risk
tenant_types.default_behavior: no public defaults through Sep 2026; risk is unrealized/forward-looking, not yet realized -- model as a rare but real tail event, not a common one

real_examples.name: Oracle-OpenAI (Stargate)
real_examples.note: largest cloud commitment on record; central 'circularity' criticism case -- OpenAI has no revenue base remotely near $300B

tenant_types.label: Neocloud / enterprise sub-tenant (e.g. Fluidstack subletting from a miner-landlord, backed by a hyperscaler)
tenant_types.credit_rating: BB/B (backed to near-hyperscaler with a backstop)

price_usd_mw_yr.source: Cipher-Fluidstack ≈$1.79M/MW/yr initial (168MW/$3B/10yr); TeraWulf-Fluidstack JV (Abernathy) ≈$2.26M/MW/yr (168MW/$9.5B/25yr, hybrid hosting+JV-profit structure)

prepayment_pct.note: backstop replaces prepayment in these deals -- see lenders.json Google-backstop entry

tenant_types.sla_penalty: liquidated damages, but real credit support comes from the third-party backstop, not tenant balance sheet
tenant_types.default_behavior: none observed; structure exists precisely because the market doesn't trust neocloud sub-tenant credit alone

real_examples.name: TeraWulf-Fluidstack JV (Abernathy)
real_examples.structure: majority-owned JV -- TeraWulf keeps majority ownership + hosting fee + JV profit share

tenant_cards.capex_credit_cap_owner_change: was 1500000 (the pack); raised to 2000000 by the owner, 28 Sep 2026 (M5 answer 1, step 3)
tenant_cards.basis: Core Scientific-CoreWeave: $1.96M/MW/yr implied, tenant funds capex up to a $1.5M/MW credit cap

tenant_cards.fictional_name: (no tenant -- sell full-stack capacity at the spot index)

penalty_pct_of_annual_contract_per_quart.source: not publicly disclosed in any reviewed press release (confidential contract exhibits); design default. Fix: Alpha 0.2 scope v1.0 §2.5 / §7 [P1] fixes it at 3% (the pack gave 1-3%)

walk_chance_late_2q.source: Alpha 0.2 scope v1.0 §2.5 / §7 [P1]: replaces the pack's flat termination_chance_at_2q_late 0.50. At 2 quarters late the tenant may walk with its type's chance (same values as tenant_types[].walk_chance_late_2q); terminations stay a tail event, liquidated damages the common case

take_or_pay_terms.real_delivery_track_record: no public example found of a hyperscaler invoking termination-for-delay against a miner-turned-AI-host through Sep 2026; model termination as a rare tail event, standard liquidated-damages as the common case

rate_usd_kwh.source: Hashrate Index: hosting rates ballooned in 2022 (power-cost spike post energy crisis); many hosts shifted to profit/revenue-share instead of flat $/kWh; Core Scientific raised to $0.10/kWh and still filed Ch.11 anyway

client_defaults.name: Compute North
client_defaults.note: fixed-rate hosting contracts prevented passing rising power costs through to clients -- a direct bankruptcy trigger, owed up to $500M
